Issued at 318 AM EDT Mon Jul 27 2026

Pattern Synopsis/Forecast: Broad upper ridge encompasses the 
southwest/southern Plains and the lower Mississippi Valley...with a 
split trough long wave trough across eastern North America. Closed 
low in the northern branch of the split trough is part of a high-
latitude block from Hudson Bay eastward across the North Atlantic. 
Long wave trough off the west coast is firing pieces of energy over 
the top of the western ridge...one such wave was moving into 
northern Manitoba with a second over southern Saskatchewan. 
Elongated latent PV anomaly around the fringes of the upper ridge 
associated with the cyclonic shear side of an anticyclonically 
curved jet extending from off the California coast...up and around 
the periphery of the ridge and diving across the Great Lakes/mid 
Atlantic.  Steep mid level lapse rates/elevated mixed layer 
spreading into the Great Lakes from the northwest...700mb 
temperatures at or above +12C knocking on Michigan's doorstep. 
Sunday evening surface analysis shows the usual summer mesoscale 
chaos: 1002mb surface low along the North Dakota/Minnesota border 
with a wavy frontal boundary extending to a 1005mb frontal wave over 
Lake Superior.  A second warm front extends southeast across 
Minnesota/Wisconsin/Illinois and into the Ohio Valley...with 70s-
lower 80s dew points pooled along and on the warm side of this 
front.  Michigan is in a narrow wedge between these two boundaries.  

Northern Manitoba short wave trough digs southeast across the Great 
Lakes today...reinforcing the southern branch of the split long wave 
trough downstream.  Overall pattern configuration doesn't look to 
change much through midweek; forecast trends continue to show a more 
blocky pattern across the Atlantic basin...with more agreement on a 
closed low developing in the southern branch over the mid Atlantic/ 
southern New England...as well as more agreement that height rises 
will push into the Great Lakes for midweek.  For the latter half of 
the week...energy undercutting the ridge may allow for some height 
falls across the eastern CONUS and some overall retrogression of the 
pattern as the ridge amplitude sharpens across the Rockies in 
response to a strong upper low moving into the Pacific Northwest/ 
British Columbia next weekend (an impressive 600dam 500mb high 
centered in the vicinity of the Four Corners next weekend).  

Low pressure moving across the Great Lakes later tonight will become 
better organized as it moves into the lower Lakes tonight...with a 
stronger pressure gradient setting up across Michigan for Tuesday as 
a result.  High pressure nudges into the upper Lakes Wednesday/ 
Thursday along with rising heights as the downstream pattern gets 
backed up.  Looking at some height falls and possibly a frontal 
passage for Friday/Saturday.  

Primary Forecast Concerns: 

Showers and thunderstorms through tonight with strong/severe 
thunderstorm potential along with a heavy rain threat: As of this 
writing (0630Z)...a narrow northwest-southeast line of convection is 
developing from southern Lake Winnipeg to northeast Wisconsin.  A 
smaller cluster of thunderstorms is dropping southeast across 
eastern Upper Michigan....also getting some radar returns east of I-
75 in northern Lower.  All of this is developing along an elevated 
instability gradient... which will be shifting across the upper 
Lakes today. Current thinking is that upstream convection will 
propagate east during the overnight hours (mid level winds are 
backing more west)...and eventually spread into northern Michigan 
this morning. It is quite possible that with surface low approaching 
this afternoon...along with larger scale forcing with digging short 
wave trough/left front quadrant jet forcing...there may be several 
clusters of storms impacting northern Michigan throughout the day 
into tonight.  Severe threat will certainly be in play today given 
magnitude of the instability and deep layer shear...have already 
popped off a few SVRs across eastern Upper this morning.  Other 
concern is heavy rain potential...especially the way upstream 
convection is lining up. As a result not going to get too cute with 
PoPs and timing...if there is a larger break in the precipitation 
then so be it...otherwise one is just asking for trouble.  Plan to 
have an explicit mention of heavy rain in the forecast through this 
evening. 

A little cooler and a little breezy Tuesday with an increasing Great 
Lakes swim risk:  Tighter pressure gradient and some momentum to mix 
down expected to result in gusty winds Tuesday from the north/ 
northwest...on the order of 20-30mph.  Higher waves in a more 
limited northerly fetch would be south of Grand Traverse Light on 
Lake Michigan (high swim risk for Manistee County...moderate for 
rest of northwest Lower shoreline counties)...and south of Thunder 
Bay Island on Lake Huron (moderate swim risk for northeast Lower 
shoreline counties).  Cold
